stories.title: Hormuz attacks hit a record as oil reaches $110
stories.body: October has seen more attacks on ships than any month since the war began on 28 February. UK Maritime Trade Operations confirmed at least 12 ships attacked in the week to 16 October, and one, the GFS Pride, sank. The US and Iran both claim to control the Strait. Brent crude reached $110 a barrel, its highest since May. Pakistan and Qatar are still passing messages, but no breakthrough is expected before the 3 November US midterms.
stories.why: Higher oil prices raise Nigeria's export earnings but also the cost of imported fuel, shipping and food.

cards.front: What price did Brent crude reach in mid-October 2026?
cards.back: $110 a barrel, its highest since May 2026.

stories.title: Ukraine retakes ground in Donetsk as US support wavers
stories.body: Ukraine said its Operation Vivaldi has retaken about 275 sq km and 16 settlements in eastern Donetsk since August, blunting Russia's push towards Lyman. President Trump declared an energy ceasefire on 11 October, but Russia then fired 850 drones and 39 missiles in a single day at energy targets. On 9 October Trump also invited Russia to sell 1.8 million tonnes of diesel on world markets. President Zelenskyy said partners did not share warning of missiles that hit a Kyiv power plant on 13 October.
stories.why: Russian fuel sales and attacks on energy supplies both move world fuel prices, which Nigeria feels at the pump.

cards.back: A counter-offensive in eastern Donetsk that retook about 275 sq km and 16 settlements from August to October 2026.

stories.title: Tinubu orders agencies to rescue all kidnap victims
stories.body: After a security meeting at the State House, Defence Minister Christopher Musa said President Tinubu had ordered security agencies to rescue all kidnapped people and dismantle terrorist and bandit camps. The meeting also looked at security for the 2027 elections. Musa said the armed forces will stay neutral and give all parties and candidates equal treatment.
stories.why: Election-season security and kidnapping are both likely interview topics.

stories.title: Bandits tax and attack villages in Niger State
stories.body: Suspected bandits killed five farmers and abducted 18 people in attacks on Fanga (Mashegu LGA) and on Kigbere and Kokani (Borgu LGA) between 9 and 12 October. Residents of Fanga said the gang had imposed levies five times and attacked again when the community could not pay. Villagers in Rukukuje, Rijau LGA, fled after reports that bandits were moving in from Zamfara.
stories.why: Bandits charging illegal levies show they are acting like a parallel government in parts of the North-central and North-west.

cards.front: What is a bandit 'levy' in Nigeria's North-west and North-central?
cards.back: Money bandit gangs force communities to pay, under threat of attack.

stories.title: Gaza ceasefire turns one, but the killing goes on
stories.body: One year after the Gaza ceasefire took effect, Gaza's Health Ministry says 1,493 people have been killed and 5,299 wounded since the truce began. More than 100 aid and rights groups say the ceasefire exists in name only. Aid trucks are entering at about a third of the agreed rate, and no international stabilisation force has deployed. Israel now controls nearly two-thirds of the Strip, more than the roughly 50 percent agreed.
stories.why: Nigeria backs a two-state solution, and the ceasefire's anniversary is a likely current-affairs question.

cards.front: About how much of Gaza did Israel control one year into the ceasefire (October 2026)?
cards.back: Nearly two-thirds, more than the roughly 50 percent agreed.

stories.title: Military: 36 terrorists killed, 50 hostages freed in a week
stories.body: Defence Headquarters said troops killed 36 terrorists and rescued at least 50 kidnapped people between 2 and 8 October. In Borno, Operation Hadin Kai repelled an ISWAP assault on Kukawa. In Kebbi, Operation Fansan Yamma killed 10 Lakurawa fighters. In Imo, troops freed 20 prospective NYSC corps members abducted on the Owerri–Onitsha Expressway. The Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, urged citizens to report terrorist collaborators.
stories.why: It shows Nigeria's security threats in every zone at once, from ISWAP in the North-east to kidnapping in the South-east.

cards.front: Which military operation covers Kebbi and the North-west against Lakurawa and bandits?
